correctness.rationale: Independently checked cell and disjoint-pair occupancy and sign cancellation, giving the normalized simplex quadratic in RESULT.md lines 36–50. Expanding that quadratic into constant, row, column and zero-margin parts gives the first exact deficit. Interpolating from the critical quadratic to the full-permutation endpoint gives the second deficit via the permutation variance. Its equality conditions force a pairwise-intersecting support and constant permutation sum, hence a whole row or column of equal masses. At criticality the only constraint besides simplex membership is zero interaction. The upper proof uses the clique support reduction by strict convexity on a pair of conflicting cells and the uniform masses on a largest matching; the only q>1 cases are (2,2) and (3,3), and q=1 only at (4,4). The sphere gives the interval. Averaging both quadratic comparison inequalities over row/column signs and permutations removes off-diagonal terms and makes the diagonal constant, proving the claimed exact Banach–Mazur distance. The supplied checker and its verification description were inspected, not executed; the proofs do not depend on exhaustive experiments. 'Positive slice' means the nonnegative simplex intersection, as the stated extremizers can include zeros.
